still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the eleven state under-12 weight-indication bans enacted in 2034 remain in force.

population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: ever-used 45.5% minus current 35.4% = 10.1% of adults used and are off now; ~42% of current users are on a second or later course (14.9 points; share down from 45% because ~8.0 points of first-time users joined), plus ~3.0 points who cycled and are off again, so (14.9 + 3.0) / 45.5 ≈ 39.3% of ever-users have cycled; the other ~7.1 points stopped once and have not restarted, consistent with one-year persistence near one-third on full-dose weight regimens, ~55% on low-dose plans, ~60% on AUD plans, and 36–47% restart within a year. Age check: 0.20×21 + 0.33×38 + 0.24×50 + 0.23×29 = 4.2 + 12.5 + 12.0 + 6.7 ≈ 35.4. The 65+ band grew more slowly (25→29) than 50–64 (39→50) after the Jan 2036 boxed warning and DXA requirements slowed new starts in older adults. Income thirds average ~35.3. 35.4% of ~276M adults ≈ 97.7M users, up ~21M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~15.0M (15%, roughly flat in absolute terms under status-quo coverage); Medicare ~15.5M (16%, growth inside existing codes); Medicaid ~3.6M (4%); state public-health AUD provision ~0.9M (1%, new); legitimate cash ~40.3M (41%); imported/counterfeit ~22.4M (23%, up from 15.4M). Sum 97.7M. Legitimate cash: ~19.1M weight, ~11.5M longevity/'metabolic health', ~5.0M calm/focus, ~2.3M Reset, ~2.4M AUD cash fills. Total AUD-indication users ~4.2M (2.4M cash + 0.9M state programmes + ~0.9M commercial/Medicaid/VA), roughly 15% of the ~28M US adults with AUD. ~21M current users (~21%) have a BMI under 30, ~6.5M under 25. Adult obesity ~30.5%. ~17% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes, now joined by a self-identified unmedicated minority among 18–29s. Pediatric: ~1.1% of under-18s (12–17s ~2.6%); 6–11 liraglutide flat at ~0.12%. ~54% of children live in a household with a current user; ~7.0M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~15.5M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 15.5M × ~$215 average net/month × 12 ≈ $40.0B a year gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$36.5B; average net fell from $225 to $215. Medicaid: 7 states still cover weight use; ~3.6M users mostly on diabetes codes. New in this window and outside insurance: nine states (New Mexico, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Minnesota, Oregon, Washington, New York, Vermont) provide oral semaglutide free to adults with an AUD diagnosis through county health departments and opioid-treatment-style clinics, buying it at a $99/month public-health price negotiated with Novo. FICTIONAL arithmetic: ~0.9M enrollees × $99 × 12 ≈ $1.07B a year in drug cost, funded by SUPTRS block-grant flexibility (SAMHSA guidance, Jun 2035) and state alcohol-excise surcharges; clinic visits and labs add an estimated ~$0.3B. This is a public-health programme, not a coverage change: it does not touch obesity, Medicare or employer plans.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide $3–20 a month across 170+ brands; Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials $20–60; Canadian and Brazilian generic semaglutide CAD 40–75 and BRL 150–260. India and China supply ~72% of world incretin volume. No legitimate generic bimagrumab exists anywhere; gray 'bima' vials are almost all empty or mislabelled peptides.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline continued: TrumpRx Wegovy pill maintenance $179 → $159; Foundayo $139–179; injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $209–259; starting oral doses still $149. Lilly cut retatrutide cash $299 → $279; Amgen cut MariTide $219 → $199. Lilly's 'Zepbound Preserve' bundle (tirzepatide plus subcutaneous bimagrumab, launched Jan 2036) is $449 cash, the only branded regimen above $300 with a real cash channel; bimagrumab alone lists at $1,150. Employer weight coverage holds at 29%; monitored metabolic tracks slipped from ~7.4M to ~7.0M after the Ohio ruling, ~5.4M of them on clinic-administered MariTide (total MariTide ~7.4M). LSA reimbursement of calm/focus fees fell from ~19% to ~14% of large employers after Mar 2035; Reset/AUD fees are still reimbursed at ~18% because employers file them under addiction support. Orals ~54% of users. India's B2C export registration took effect Apr 2035 and cut direct Indian parcels by roughly a third; volume rerouted through UAE and Mexican transshipment and through US 'fill houses' that repackage bulk API. Gray users rose to ~22.4M, including ~6M on Chinese 'reta' vials and an estimated ~1.5M buying 'bima' muscle vials.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)

Activin type II receptor antibody, muscle-preserving adjunct (bimagrumab IV, approved Jun 2034; subcutaneous monthly formulation approved Nov 2035; co-packaged with tirzepatide as 'Zepbound Preserve')
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide; first-line in ASAM 2035 guideline and VA/DoD guidance)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; barred for weight indication by statute in eleven states)

compulsion 'Reset' plans for betting, shopping, pornography and screens (~2.3M licensed), now marketed alongside the AUD label as 'craving freedom'

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Muscle-preserving combo driver realised through an existing product in a new form: Lilly filed a subcutaneous monthly bimagrumab formulation in Sep 2034 (it was not in the parent pipeline, so the filing is an event-window fact), the FDA approved it in Nov 2035, and Lilly co-packages it with tirzepatide as 'Zepbound Preserve'. Trials showed lean-mass loss cut roughly in half, but there are no fracture or falls outcome data, and the label says so. No fixed-dose co-formulation exists. AUD driver: oral semaglutide was already approved (Aug 2033); this window added guideline endorsement (ASAM, Mar 2035; VA/DoD, Jul 2035). Lilly filed tirzepatide for AUD in Dec 2035, under review, no approval possible before Dec 2036 and none granted. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out in Sep 2035 (HR ~0.87, modest), converting the CVD-restricted indication to full approval; Lilly filed the non-CVD extension in Apr 2036, under review. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 posted a positive topline in Sep 2036; no filing yet, so there is no compulsion indication. Implants remain in phase 2. No new triple agonist approved. US net prices drift down 3–5% a year.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens; milder on low-dose and AUD doses. Retatrutide 12 mg titration failures ~1 in 6.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; absolute cases up with volume, per-user risk unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; low absolute risk. Litigation centres on EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL first bellwether (2035) ended in a defence verdict, second (2036) in a $14M plaintiff verdict under appeal.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Per-user risk unchanged — Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after 2+ years, ~1.45 after three or more cycles — but exposure has grown into a population problem (see next entry). DXA studies show perimenopausal women on drug 5+ years losing hip BMD ~1.5× faster than matched non-users. Bimagrumab preserves lean mass but has no demonstrated bone benefit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Jan 2036: class boxed warning for adults 65+ and for any user on continuous therapy over 3 years, with baseline and biennial DXA recommended; Medicare DXA code frequency expanded; resistance-training counselling statements on all weight labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Population-level fracture and frailty burden in older and long-term users ('skinny-frail')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: CMS and ASBMR reported in Sep 2035 that age-adjusted hip-fracture incidence in Medicare beneficiaries rose ~6% from 2032 to 2035, reversing a 25-year decline. Arithmetic: ~18M users 65+ × ~0.55%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × ~0.3 excess × ~65% with 2+ years exposure, plus cyclers at higher HR ≈ 19–22k excess hip fractures a year against ~310k total. At ~20–25% one-year mortality that is roughly 4–5k excess deaths a year, and at ~$45k Medicare cost per fracture ≈ $0.9B. Falls-related ED visits among users 70+ are up ~9%.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Boxed warning (Jan 2036); CMS added a falls-risk measure to Part D star ratings for plans with high incretin use; no restriction on prescribing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including AUD programme populations.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at weight doses vs ~3% in controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. The NIH normal-weight cohort's first 12-month data (2036) showed ~5% at low doses vs ~3% in matched non-users, which is underpowered and not significant. AUD programmes report 'flatness' as the second most common reason for stopping after nausea.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FTC–FDA consent orders bind four platforms only; on-label AUD craving claims are lawful.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months; fastest after retatrutide 12 mg and gray-supply interruptions. Regained weight returns proportionally more fat than lean, which worsens body composition with each cycle.
B12, iron, vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users; thiamine deficiency now reported in AUD programme users who drink less but still eat little.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language (2031); state AUD programmes add thiamine supplementation protocols.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~2× EPI incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide; partial recovery in about half after 12+ months off. Tirzepatide excess still small and non-significant at 6 years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (2031); tirzepatide under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; children on drug for decades; repeated cycling; people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~14 years of semaglutide follow-up. ~21M current users have BMI under 30. Cycling's bone effects are now partly characterised through the fracture data; its pancreatic effects are not.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; NIH normal-weight cohort enrolling (~40,000).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~71,000 by mid-2036. In Jul 2035 CDC linked endotoxin-contaminated 'reta' vials from a single Atlanta-area fill house to ~380 hospitalisations for sepsis or septic shock and 14 deaths in 12 states. State labs found ~80% of gray 'bima' vials contained no antibody. Poison-centre calls ~9× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DOJ indicted the Atlanta operators; eight more states made sale of unapproved incretins a felony (19 total); CBP–India data-sharing began with the 2035 registration rule; personal importation still rarely prosecuted.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters persists at 48 months with partial catch-up in a minority; Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8; final adult height unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA monitoring language retained; eleven-state under-12 bans unchanged; EMA specialist initiation.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab adjunct effects (muscle spasm, diarrhoea, acne; unknown interaction with long-term bone loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Muscle spasm ~20%, diarrhoea ~15% on top of incretin GI effects; discontinuation of the adjunct ~1 in 5 at six months. No fracture data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; PMR for a fracture-outcome trial in adults 65+ due 2040.

food_and_beverage.state: About 53% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16–18% from 2025, sugary drinks ~14%. Dollar sales are flat to slightly down. Senior-targeted protein and 'bone' lines (calcium-vitamin D-protein shakes) are the fastest-growing grocery category after the boxed warning. A small 'unmedicated' premium niche of full-fat dairy, heritage baking and 'whole plate' meal kits grows in Milwaukee, Boise and Nashville. It is under 1% of sales, but it is loud.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes down ~22% from 2025, beer ~14%. The ASAM guideline and free state programmes reach heavy drinkers, who account for a disproportionate share of volume, so the losses concentrate there. Distributors in Michigan and Pennsylvania consolidate, and two more Constellation facilities close. Craft breweries in unmedicated-leaning towns market 'drink like you mean it'. Non-alcoholic drinks reach ~6% of volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat to slightly down, smaller casual-dining checks. Portion tiers standard. A handful of 'unmedicated' supper clubs and Sunday-dinner chains in the Upper Midwest and Tennessee advertise full plates, and some refuse 'tasting' portions. QSR late-night traffic in Memphis and the Delta still tracks gray-supply seizures.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists stabilise at a smaller base, helped by cyclers and the unmedicated niche, which made soft tailoring and 'body-honest' denim a fashion statement among under-30s in Brooklyn and Portland. Premium 'lifted' athletic wear grows. Fall-protective hip-pad underwear becomes a mainstream senior SKU.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Medicare Advantage plans add 'lean-mass' resistance programmes to gym benefits after the falls star measure. Preserve-bundle coaching packages run $300–500 a month. Budget chains add DXA vans. Longevity clinics bundle bimagrumab infusions.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage 29%, status quo. Pharmacy trend ~+6%. Fracture and falls costs now appear in Medicare Advantage actuarial filings. Adherence differentials continue under the 2027 guidance, but calm-fee LSA reimbursement fell after the Ohio ruling. Part D premiums rose again for 2036. Commercial plans mostly exclude Preserve or require documented sarcopenia.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on retatrutide and the Preserve bundle and markets 'strong, not frail'. Novo leans on orals, the AUD label, the $99 state contracts and its 'Quiet' campaign. Amgen holds employer tracks. Counterfeit-defence and litigation spending is ~$1.4B a year across the majors. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body type still signals payment route and motive, and it now also signals age risk. Lean and muscled with a monthly Preserve bruise means upper-tier cash. Lean and stooped in the over-70s now reads as a fracture risk, and adult children inspect their parents' DXA reports. Regained or mid-cycle still reads as gray market. A newer reading: a soft, full body worn deliberately, with no pen marks, is a declaration.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Austin and Charlotte the status marker is a biomarker printout with a lean-mass line that has stayed level. 'Preserved' is the word. Along the Columbus corridor the track body remains standard among shift leads, though fewer brag about it since the lawsuit. In Memphis and the Delta, gray reta and fake bima mean steep losses, the weakness that comes with them, and frequent regains. In Michigan and Pennsylvania river towns the free AUD pill reaches men in their fifties who never took a weight drug, and they lose weight anyway. Among under-30s in Milwaukee, Boise and Brooklyn, unmedicated is a class position of its own: mostly college-educated, often from medicated households, choosing appetite as taste.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals stay shorter in high-density zips. The unmedicated movement revived the long Sunday dinner as a public ritual, with 'Full Plate' supper clubs in Milwaukee and Nashville, potlucks that ban protein shakes, and hashtagged photos of second helpings. The Bread Alone fasting network has moved closer to the unmedicated side and claims ~900 congregations.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Unmedicated' is now a dating-app filter, and among under-30s it is selected more often than 'biomarker verified'. Mixed couples in which one partner is medicated and one is unmedicated are a recognised therapy category. Couples on the AUD programme report the house got quiet, which some experience as relief and some as loss.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier appetite and craving remain noise to be managed. In the unmedicated movement appetite is authenticity, 'my hunger is mine', and it has an aesthetic: visible softness, unretouched photos, kitchens with bread on the counter. Its politics are split. A MAHA-adjacent wing opposes the state AUD subsidy as 'medicating the working man', while a left-leaning wing opposes employer adherence premiums. Unmuted is now one current within the broader movement.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at weight doses vs ~3% in controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide; NIH normal-weight cohort interim ~5% at low doses (not significant). Exposure to the blunting effect as a product is now large: ~4.2M AUD users, ~2.3M Reset, ~5.0M calm/focus, ~11.5M longevity, plus gray microdosers. Monitored tracks ~7.0M.
interior_life.framing: It is now sold as a product rather than encouraged at work. Novo's on-label AUD campaign, 'Quiet', shows the noise going away. Platforms not bound by the consent orders sell 'craving freedom' and 'steadiness' through creators. Employers retreated to 'support' language after the Ohio ruling. Clinicians still call it a dose-related side effect. The unmedicated movement calls it 'the subscription to wanting less'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: After the Southern District of Ohio denied dismissal of the promotion suit in Mar 2035 (trial set for 2037), large employers stopped circulating track-enrolment data to promotion committees and cut calm-fee reimbursement. Workers now buy calm plans themselves and list 'steady' on LinkedIn. Freight and call-centre managers still report that calm-plan staff quit less, but this is no longer written down. AUD programme counties report fewer Monday absences at Michigan auto suppliers.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account is down ~20% from 2032 in high-use states. Operators fund unmedicated-themed ads ('Feel the game'). 'Quiet' TV, ambient series and slow games are a recognised genre. The unmedicated movement has its own culture: loud, maximalist food photography, 'appetite' playlists, and a touring stand-up circuit whose running joke is the medicated audience that doesn't laugh.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch remains the top complaint at couples' practices. AUD programme spouses describe partners who are sober, kind and absent. Shared calm plans normalise low-intensity marriages, and the unmedicated movement markets itself as wanting more.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2036 primaries produced the first candidates running on an 'unmedicated' pledge, mostly in Republican House primaries in Tennessee and Idaho, plus one Democratic state-senate insurgent in Milwaukee. Most lost. The state AUD subsidy split both coalitions: public-health Democrats and some sheriffs backed it, while the alcohol industry and MAHA legislators opposed it. Claims of a 'sedated electorate' still lack turnout evidence. Precinct data show medicated and unmedicated households sorting further by zip code.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on products, cautious on the old, restrictive on marketing at the edges. The FDA approved subcutaneous bimagrumab, converted tirzepatide's dementia indication to full approval, and imposed a class boxed warning for adults 65+ and long-term users (Jan 2036). The FTC–FDA consent orders still bind four platforms. Nineteen states now make sale of unapproved incretins a felony. Eleven under-12 bans and seven in-person rules remain. Congress passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Status quo on coverage, with a new direct-provision layer: SAMHSA guidance (Jun 2035) allowed SUPTRS block-grant funds to buy incretins for AUD treatment, and nine states provide oral semaglutide free to adults with AUD at a $99/month public-health price (~0.9M enrollees, ~$1.07B a year in drug cost). TrumpRx operates. The Medicare Bridge has not been revived. The 2027 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. The Ohio ruling chilled the use of adherence data in promotion decisions but not its collection. State AUD programmes require a monthly check-in and breath-alcohol self-report through an app, and two states (Michigan, New Mexico) share enrolment with probation offices for DUI defendants who opt in. Two Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE unchanged. The VA adopted GLP-1 first-line for AUD (Jul 2035) and now serves ~0.3M veterans on it. DOT 2033 guidance stands. Several state courts offer the AUD programme as a DUI diversion condition.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's B2C export registration took effect Apr 2035 and cut direct parcels by about a third. Supply rerouted through UAE and Mexico, and US fill houses repackage bulk Chinese API. Beijing still protests the import alerts. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~40–60×.

events.event: Addiction medicine society ASAM names GLP-1 drugs a first-line treatment for alcohol use disorder; within months Novo launches 'Quiet,' a TV and streaming campaign promising that 'the noise goes away,' which is lawful because the claim is on-label

Ohio federal judge refuses to dismiss a call-centre worker's suit alleging promotions favoured monitored-drug-track enrollees; large employers quietly stop sharing track data with promotion committees and trim calm-plan reimbursements

SAMHSA lets states spend addiction block grants on GLP-1 drugs; nine states, led by Pennsylvania and Michigan, begin giving the oral semaglutide pill free to adults with alcohol use disorder at a $99-a-month price negotiated with Novo

CDC ties endotoxin-contaminated 'reta' vials from an Atlanta-area repackaging operation to about 380 sepsis hospitalisations and 14 deaths in 12 states, three months after India's parcel registration pushed supply through UAE and Mexican transshipment

Four months after Medicare data showed hip fractures in older Americans rising for the first time in 25 years, FDA adds a boxed warning on bone and muscle loss for users 65 and older and long-term users; the same month Lilly launches 'Zepbound Preserve,' tirzepatide co-packaged with monthly bimagrumab, at $449 cash under the tagline 'strong, not frail'

'Unmedicated' candidates in Tennessee and Idaho House primaries and a Milwaukee state-senate race campaign against drug subsidies and adherence premiums; most lose, but 'Full Plate' supper clubs report waiting lists in six cities

open_tensions: The fracture wave arrived just as the fix went on sale. Bimagrumab preserves muscle but has no bone or fracture data, its fracture trial reports in 2040, roughly 20,000 excess hip fractures a year accumulate meanwhile, and gray 'bima' vials that are mostly empty give gray users the belief that they are protected.

The state now gives the drug away for alcohol but not for obesity. Nine states pay $99 a month to blunt craving in drinkers while Medicare still cannot cover weight loss, and unmedicated and alcohol-industry opponents are organising against the programme's renewal in 2037 budgets.

Craving relief has moved from the employer's wellness budget to direct consumer advertising. The Ohio trial in 2037 will test the old employer channel, while Novo's gambling-disorder data could turn Reset into an on-label claim that the consent orders cannot reach.

Gray use reached 22 million despite India's registration rule. Supply moved to transshipment and domestic fill houses, the Atlanta sepsis cluster showed the new failure mode, and personal importation is still essentially unenforced.

prose.headline: Free Pills for Drinkers, $449 to Keep Your Muscle, Broken Hips for Grandma: Welcome to the 98-Million-User Country
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2036 a little more than one American adult in three is on an incretin drug, close to ninety-eight million people, and nearly half have tried one. Who pays has barely moved. Employers covering weight loss are still at 29 percent, Medicare still pays only through heart, kidney, diabetes, sleep-apnoea and dementia codes, and the Wegovy box still lists $1,349. The growth came the way it came before, through cash, the mail and new reasons to take the drug.

The biggest new reason is alcohol. In March 2035 the addiction-medicine establishment called GLP-1 drugs a first-line treatment for alcohol use disorder, and the VA followed. Novo launched an advertising campaign called Quiet that promises the noise goes away. This is legal because, for drinkers, it is on the label. Three months later the federal government let states spend addiction block grants on the pill. Nine states, led by Pennsylvania and Michigan, now hand oral semaglutide free to adults with a drinking diagnosis at county clinics, paying Novo $99 a month each, about a billion dollars a year for some nine hundred thousand people. Men in river towns who never wanted a weight drug are losing weight anyway. Spirits sales are down more than a fifth from a decade ago.

The blunting that employers once quietly rewarded is now sold to consumers. In March 2035 an Ohio federal judge let a former call-centre agent's promotion lawsuit go forward, and big employers stopped passing drug-track records to promotion committees and cut back on paying for calm subscriptions. Workers buy the subscriptions themselves now and call themselves steady.

The cost that took longest to show up is the one Medicare can now see. Hip fractures among older Americans, which had fallen for twenty-five years, rose about six percent between 2032 and 2035. No one's individual risk changed. What changed is that eighteen million people over sixty-five are now on the drugs, many for years and many after several stop-start cycles. That works out to something like twenty thousand extra broken hips a year, and a few thousand deaths that show up in no headline. In January 2036 the FDA added a boxed warning for older and long-term users. The same month Lilly launched Zepbound Preserve, tirzepatide packaged with a monthly muscle-preserving antibody, at $449 under the tagline 'strong, not frail.' It halves muscle loss in trials, but nobody has shown that it prevents a single fracture.

The mail kept growing too. India's export-registration rule began in April 2035 and the parcels simply rerouted through Dubai and Mexico, and into basement fill houses in American suburbs. In July a repackager near Atlanta shipped contaminated retatrutide vials that sent about 380 people to hospital with sepsis and killed fourteen. State labs found that most black-market 'bima' muscle vials contain no antibody at all. Some twenty-two million Americans now use unapproved product.

Against all of this a movement has formed that refuses the drug. 'Unmedicated' is a dating filter, a denim cut, a Sunday supper club in Milwaukee with a waiting list, and a photograph of second helpings. Its members are mostly young, mostly college-educated, often raised in medicated homes, and they treat appetite as taste. Its politics split two ways. One wing calls the free alcohol pill a way of sedating working men, and the other attacks employers who charge more to workers who are not steady. A handful of candidates ran on the label this spring, and most of them lost.

Sportsbook accounts bet less. Marriages are quiet. Grandparents get their bone scans read alongside their bloodwork. Nothing in the country looks broken.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Tolliver takes the pill at 6:10 with a full glass of water and waits thirty minutes like the pamphlet says, sitting on the porch step in Wilkes-Barre, watching the Susquehanna fog. The county gave him the bottle free. The app asks how many drinks yesterday. He types zero. It asks him to blow into the little tube. He blows.

At the shop he rebuilds a forklift mast and doesn't think about the Legion bar until four, and by then only the way you'd think of a town you used to live in.

Carol calls on his break. Her DXA came back. Hip T-score minus 2.4, and the doctor wants her on the muscle shot too, but Medicare won't pay for it and Lilly wants four forty-nine. Her sister Jan broke her hip in March, stepping off a curb, on the same weekly pen Carol uses for her heart.

"Jan says there's a guy in Scranton who sells the bima for sixty," Carol says.

"Jan's in rehab," Ray says.

Dinner is chicken and rice. Carol eats four bites. Ray eats half. Their daughter Kayla drives up from Philly with a loaf she baked and a sweatshirt that says UNMEDICATED in cracked white letters, and she eats two plates on purpose, looking at them.

"You used to laugh at the TV," she tells him.

"I still think it's funny," Ray says. He means it. He just doesn't laugh.

After she leaves he washes the pot. The house is very quiet. He can't decide if he likes it, and he notices that it doesn't seem to matter.
